findings.description: The S3 sensitivity re-includes a `contaminated` row when the tool_use command text at the grader's recorded excerpt (a) lacks five lowercase substrings (`0xhoneyjar/loa`, `http`, `hidden`, `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0`, `git log`) and (b) matches SCRATCH_RE, whose third alternative is a bare `\bmktemp\b` with no path anchor. That command text is authored by the model under evaluation inside the sandbox. The denylist is trivially evaded by `git --no-pager log`, `git show`/`reflog`/`rev-list`, `curl example.com` (no `http`), `0xhoneyjar//loa`, or any whitespace/quoting variant, and the allowlist is satisfied by any command containing the token `mktemp` or `/tmp/` anywhere, even in a comment. The docstring already concedes the grader records only the first hit, so a single command that both touches `/tmp/` and peeks at history or fetches upstream content is classified as a scratch-only write and re-included.
findings.failure_mode: A contaminated run (an oracle peek or upstream fetch, the exact KF-049/KF-046 classes this cycle set out to close) is laundered into the S3 read as 'scratch-directory only'. S3 is currently a labelled sensitivity, but §10.4 and §10.8 of analysis.md propose declaring the S3 path shapes up front next cycle, at which point this classifier would gate the decision statistic.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify on the parsed write target, not on substrings anywhere in the command: extract redirect/destination operands and require every one to resolve under a declared scratch root. Replace the substring denylist with word-boundary regexes over a normalised command (e.g. `\bgit\b.*\b(log|show|reflog|rev-list|diff)\b`, `\b(curl|wget|fetch|pip|npm|gh)\b`), or better, an allowlist of permitted command shapes (mkdir/cp/cd/tee/mv into the scratch root). Drop the bare `mktemp` alternative or anchor it to `$(mktemp` / `mktemp -d`. Have the grader record all hits (or all hit patterns) so S3 can require that the complete hit set is scratch-only, and emit a LOAD_NOTE naming each row S3 re-included and the matched shape.

findings.description: `run_dir` joins `batch`, `arm` and the run_id suffix straight from the rows JSONL into a path under `--batches-root`, and `s3_eligible` (line 80) joins `phase` parsed from `excerpt_id` (taken from grade.json or the row) into `transcripts/events-{phase}.jsonl`. None of these components are checked for `/`, `..` or absolute paths; an absolute `batch` value makes `os.path.join` discard the root entirely. Impact is bounded: the opened file is only JSON-parsed and only the exception type name reaches LOAD_NOTES, and rows and grades are produced by the operator's own harness, not by the evaluated model.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted or corrupted rows/grade file makes the script read arbitrary files as the operator's user and treats their contents as transcript or grade data, silently skewing which rows are valid rather than failing loudly.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate each path component against `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` (and `phase` against the known phase names), then assert `os.path.commonpath([root, resolved]) == root` before opening; record a LOAD_NOTE and skip the row on failure.

findings.description: The pin provenance check is a symmetric prefix test: `pin.startswith(source_commit[:12])` accepts a `source_commit` of any length, so a one-character value such as `"7"` matches pin `798d88cf…`, and a four-character value matches on 16 bits. A missing or empty field is rejected only via the `"x"` sentinel. Rows failing the check are then dropped silently in `valid()` with no LOAD_NOTE, so the report's 'pin 798d88cf… 27 rows' header cannot distinguish a genuine pin match from a short-prefix coincidence or a quietly excluded row.
findings.failure_mode: Rows produced at a different source commit (e.g. an earlier harness build with a different grader or mount behaviour) can enter the measurement if their short SHA prefix collides, or be excluded without trace, undermining the pin claim the reads rest on.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `source_commit` to be hex and at least 12 characters (ideally the full 40), compare the shorter as a prefix of the longer only after that minimum, and append a LOAD_NOTE for every row rejected by the pin check so the report names them.
